_readme: Role profiles for the Joiner/Mover/Leaver lifecycle (roadmap v2-1).
A profile is the DESIRED STATE of an identity, expressed once and applied to
every service. The lifecycle engine reads this file, compares it against what
each service actually reports, and applies only the differences.
Every group named here already exists in configs/keycloak/realm-export.json.
Profiles describe how to reach the seeded RBAC model; they do not invent a
parallel one. Authorization stays group-based: the engine never grants a realm
role directly to a user, because in this realm the groups carry the roles.
JSON rather than YAML so the file parses with the Python standard library and
is checked by the existing CI 'JSON' job. Comments live in _readme / summary
The 'effective_roles' list is DOCUMENTATION of what the group grants, used to
render the operator-facing access diff. It is never written to Keycloak - the
engine reads real role mappings back from the API when it verifies.
Gitea has no organisation in a stock v1 lab, so the engine creates this one
on first use and reconciles the teams below. Doing it here rather than in
scripts/init-gitea.sh keeps `docker compose up -d` byte-for-byte unchanged.
gitea.organization_description: Teams provisioned by the identity lifecycle engine.
